claims.text: The default Service type is ClusterIP. A NodePort Service (type: NodePort) keeps a cluster IP, selector and ports like a ClusterIP Service and additionally opens the same port on every node; connections to that port on any node are forwarded to one of the Service's ready Pods.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Services > Service type > type: NodePort ('each node proxies that port (the same port number on every Node) into your Service'; 'also allocates a cluster IP')

claims.text: The node port number is stored in the Service's spec.ports[].nodePort.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services > type: NodePort ('reports that port in its .spec.ports[*].nodePort field'); scripts/k8s/service-types.sh line 22 jsonpath

claims.text: If nodePort is not set, the control plane allocates a free port from the range set by --service-node-port-range, default 30000-32767; each Service gets its own node port, so two Services get different numbers.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services > type: NodePort ('allocates a port from a range specified by --service-node-port-range flag (default: 30000-32767)'; Choosing your own port)

claims.text: kube-proxy writes rules for the node port on each node alongside the cluster IP rules; a connection to any node's address on the node port goes to one ready Pod, which may run on another node (default externalTrafficPolicy Cluster, not taught).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Virtual IPs and Service Proxies > iptables proxy mode ('same basic flow executes when traffic comes in through a type: NodePort Service'); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/service-types.txt

claims.text: A LoadBalancer Service gets a cluster IP and, by default, a node port (spec.allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts defaults to true; field not taught), and asks for an external load balancer.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services > type: LoadBalancer; 'Load balancer NodePort allocation' (allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts defaults to true)

claims.text: Kubernetes does not itself create the external load balancer: a controller (a program watching objects in a control loop) that not every cluster runs, on a cloud usually one the provider supplies (cloud-controller-manager, optional), provisions it; it sends traffic to the nodes.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services > type: LoadBalancer ('you must provide one'); Overview > Components (cloud-controller-manager optional); Architecture > Controllers

claims.text: The controller writes the provisioned address into the Service's status (.status.loadBalancer), and kubectl get service shows it in the EXTERNAL-IP column; until then it shows <pending>.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services > type: LoadBalancer ('Information about the provisioned balancer is published in the Service's .status.loadBalancer field'); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/service-types.txt

claims.text: kind runs cluster nodes as Docker containers and runs no controller that provisions LoadBalancer addresses, so on donhang (with the later module's address component removed) EXTERNAL-IP stays <pending>, while the cluster IP and node port still answer.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: LoadBalancer (needs cloud-provider-kind or another component); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/service-types.txt (<pending>, both wget calls answer)

claims.text: A cluster outside a cloud needs its own component to hand out LoadBalancer addresses.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services > type: LoadBalancer ('you must provide one'); outline item 5

claims.text: The staging cluster donhang-staging publishes the Gateway on 127.0.0.1:18080 (HTTP) and 127.0.0.1:18443 (HTTPS) on the learner's machine.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang STAGE.md at stage-3, section 'Clusters and their resources'

claims.text: donhang has one control-plane node (donhang-control-plane) and two workers. In service-types.sh at stage-3, both echo-ip Pods run on workers, the control-plane node runs none, and a wget from the client Pod to donhang-control-plane's address on the node port is answered by an echo-ip Pod.
kubectl get service shows PORT(S) as '<port>:<nodePort>/TCP' for NodePort and LoadBalancer Services, and CLUSTER-IP filled for both.
echo-nodeport.yaml and echo-loadbalancer.yaml use selector app=echo-ip, port 80, targetPort 8080, with type NodePort (no nodePort) and type LoadBalancer respectively.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/k8s/lessons/echo-nodeport.yaml and echo-loadbalancer.yaml at stage-3

claims.text: show prints a command after '$' then runs it; service-types.sh rebuilds donhang if gone, starts echo-ip and a client Pod, removes the later module's address component, and first deletes both Services left by an earlier run. wget -qO- prints only the response body.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang scripts/k8s/service-types.sh lines 6-19, scripts/lib/network-lessons.sh at stage-3; BusyBox wget -q, -O-

claims.text: An Ingress routes HTTP requests to Services by host and path; NodePort and LoadBalancer types only open a port or request an address for one Service.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Services > Ingress; lesson k8s.l2.ingress

claims.text: On donhang (kube-proxy in iptables mode), a Service's cluster IP is not assigned to any host; it exists only as the destination matched by kube-proxy's rules on each node, so a machine outside the cluster has no route to it.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Virtual IPs and Service Proxies ('Service IPs are not actually answered by a single host'); lesson k8s.l3.kube-proxy claim 1

claims.text: A Pod in donhang reaches the nodes' addresses (the client wget to donhang-control-plane answers); whether the host machine can reach kind node container addresses depends on how Docker runs them. Staging publishes its ports to 127.0.0.1 instead.
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/service-types.txt; kind docs: Known Issues / LoadBalancer (Docker Desktop networks not routable from host); deploy/tofu/modules/kind-cluster/main.tf listen_address
